svg.title: A Cohort Funnel That Rejects Weak Inventory Early
svg.desc: diagram id: diag-02-serial-lot-conversion-funnel; chart type: funnel; title: A Cohort Funnel That Rejects Weak Inventory Early; subtitle: One acquisition cohort; each later stage is a subset of the preceding stage.; chapter number: 6; epistemic tag: illustrative_model; assumptions note: Illustrative cohort of 100 distinct candidate lots followed over 3–9 months, not a monthly sales forecast. One opportunity identifier persists through all stages; repeat inquiries do not create new lots. Counts do not establish prices, annual revenue, or realized margin.; caption: Four completed sales from 100 sourced opportunities represent 4% cohort conversion, not four sales during the launch sprint.; stages: label: Identified resale lots; value: 100 lots | Starting acquisition cohort; numeric value: 100.0; detail: Log 100 distinct serial-defined lots with a named seller, device family, location, asking terms, and evidence of ownership authority; remove duplicate listings before counting.; label: Documented screening passes; value: 60 lots | 60% of starting cohort; numeric value: 60.0; detail: Retain 60 of the original 100 after checking provenance, recall status, manufacturer support, and availability of decontamination and service records; exclude undocumented inventory.; label: Technical and economic passes; value: 30 lots | 50% of preceding stage; numeric value: 30.0; detail: Retain 30 of those 60 after qualified inspection, landed-cost estimates, parts availability, and buyer-price comparisons; reject lots whose credible repair exposure erases contribution.; label: Acquired buyer-backed lots; value: 12 lots | 40% of preceding stage; numeric value: 12.0; detail: Acquire 12 of those 30 within the working-capital limit after documenting qualified buyer interest and enforceable purchase terms; buyer interest alone is neither a sale nor cash.; label: Accepted and settled sales; value: 4 lots | 33.3% of preceding stage; numeric value: 4.0; detail: Close four of the 12 acquired lots after testing, delivery, acceptance, and payment settlement. The other eight remain open cohort inventory or documented dispositions; they are not counted as completed sales.

text.title: A Cohort Funnel That Rejects Weak Inventory Early
text.tspan: A Cohort Funnel That Rejects Weak Inventory Early

rect.title: label: Identified resale lots; value: 100 lots | Starting acquisition cohort; numeric value: 100.0; detail: Log 100 distinct serial-defined lots with a named seller, device family, location, asking terms, and evidence of ownership authority; remove duplicate listings before counting.

label: Documented screening passes; value: 60 lots | 60% of starting cohort; numeric value: 60.0; detail: Retain 60 of the original 100 after checking provenance, recall status, manufacturer support, and availability of decontamination and service records; exclude undocumented inventory.

label: Technical and economic passes; value: 30 lots | 50% of preceding stage; numeric value: 30.0; detail: Retain 30 of those 60 after qualified inspection, landed-cost estimates, parts availability, and buyer-price comparisons; reject lots whose credible repair exposure erases contribution.

label: Acquired buyer-backed lots; value: 12 lots | 40% of preceding stage; numeric value: 12.0; detail: Acquire 12 of those 30 within the working-capital limit after documenting qualified buyer interest and enforceable purchase terms; buyer interest alone is neither a sale nor cash.

label: Accepted and settled sales; value: 4 lots | 33.3% of preceding stage; numeric value: 4.0; detail: Close four of the 12 acquired lots after testing, delivery, acceptance, and payment settlement. The other eight remain open cohort inventory or documented dispositions; they are not counted as completed sales.

text.title: Assumptions: Illustrative cohort of 100 distinct candidate lots followed over 3–9 months, not a monthly sales forecast. One opportunity identifier persists through all stages; repeat inquiries do not create new lots. Counts do not establish prices, annual revenue, or realized margin.
